summary: Defines a new MIKEY General Extension payload for carrying the key messages, reporting messages and parental control messages defined in the Open Mobile Alliance's BCAST Service and Content protection specification. This is an informational document that obsoletes RFC 4909.

eli5.summary: Mobile TV needs secret keys delivered to phones. This memo adds a new kind of envelope in a key-delivery protocol so those keys and related messages can be carried.

questions: what is the mikey general extension payload
what is oma bcast mikey type 5
subtitle: A new MIKEY payload type that carries mobile broadcast key and parental control messages.

tldr.problem: The Open Mobile Alliance's BCAST Service and Content Protection specification defines key messages and related messages that need a way to travel inside MIKEY. Newer messages had been created since RFC 4909.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC uses MIKEY's General Extension payload with a new type, 5, and a one-byte subtype: LTKM is 1, STKM is 2, LTKM Reporting is 3 and Parental Control is 4. The contents of each subtype are defined by the OMA specification, not here.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 4909 by adding subtypes 3 and 4 without changing the values 4909 assigned. The payload must be integrity protected and must not carry confidential data in the clear.

facts.label: Subtypes
facts.value: LTKM 1, STKM 2, LTKM Reporting 3, Parental Control 4

today: RFC 5410 is Informational. It obsoletes RFC 4909 and has been updated by RFC 6309.

sections.title: Background and Purpose
sections.content:
MIKEY (Multimedia Internet KEYing, RFC 3830) defines a General Extension payload so that MIKEY can be extended without allocating a new payload type. It can appear in any MIKEY message and is part of the authenticated or signed data. It has an 8-bit type field whose values are managed by IANA.

The Open Mobile Alliance (OMA) Broadcast (BCAST) group's Service and Content Protection specification uses four kinds of message: a short-term key message (STKM), a long-term key message (LTKM), an LTKM reporting message and a parental control message. This document specifies how to carry them in the General Extension payload. Any keys tied to the attributes, such as a Parental Control Pincode, stay in the MIKEY KEMAC payload.
sections.eli5: MIKEY is a mail service for secret keys, with a spare envelope for new uses. This memo defines a new use of that envelope for mobile TV messages.

sections.title: The OMA BCAST General Extension Payload
sections.content:
The payload is the General Extension with Type 5, called the OMA BCAST MIKEY General Extension. It has a Next Payload field, an 8-bit Type, a Length, and then a variable-length OMA BCAST Data Subtype field. Next Payload and Length are defined in Section 6.15 of RFC 3830. Type 5 is for OMA BCAST Service and Content Protection using the Smartcard Profile.

The data field begins with an 8-bit Subtype followed by variable-length subtype-specific data. Four subtypes are defined: 1 for LTKM, 2 for STKM, 3 for LTKM Reporting and 4 for Parental Control. What goes inside each is defined in Section 6 of the OMA BCAST specification.
sections.eli5: The envelope has a label saying it is for mobile TV, and a smaller label saying which of four letters is inside.

sections.title: Interoperability
sections.content: Interoperability spans several standards bodies, with OMA BCAST 1.0 enabler compliance the key aspect, so it is up to OMA test planning to verify compliance of implementations. The RFC says this payload type assignment does not change MIKEY beyond RFC 3830 and RFC 4563.
sections.eli5: Whether different phones and servers work together is checked by the group that wrote the mobile TV rules, not by this memo.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The General Extension payload is part of the authenticated or signed data in MIKEY. The OMA BCAST payload only needs integrity protection, and it SHALL be integrity protected. Keys or any parameters needing confidentiality MUST NOT be included in the payload. If confidential data is to be transported this way, it MUST be encrypted and encapsulated independently. MIKEY's replay protection also covers the General Extension payload.
sections.eli5: The envelope is sealed so nobody can change it, but secrets must never be written on the outside. Secrets go in their own locked box inside.

sections.title: IANA Assignments and Changes from RFC 4909
sections.content:
IANA allocated type 5 from the General Extensions payload name space for OMA BCAST, as requested by RFC 4909. It also created a name space for OMA BCAST payload subtype values, with LTKM (1) and STKM (2) from RFC 4909, and has now allocated LTKM Reporting (3) and Parental Control (4).

The OMA specification contains messages created after RFC 4909 was written. This document only adds the assignments needed for them and makes no change to values RFC 4909 assigned.
sections.eli5: The number registry gets two new entries, 3 and 4. The old entries stay as they were.
